oewn-02675578-v.learner: to be enough, or good enough, either in how much there is or in how good it is.
examples: A few kind words will answer; there is no need for a long letter.

oewn-01186429-v.learner: to be good enough for something, or to meet what it needs or do the job it is meant for.
examples: This small room will answer our needs for now.

oewn-02751892-v.learner: to be the one who is responsible for something, or who must explain it and face what follows.
examples: He will have to answer for what he has done.

oewn-00816833-v.learner: to defend yourself against a charge or a point in an argument, or to show that it is wrong.
examples: She answered the charges against her one by one.

oewn-02664648-v.learner: to match something, or to be in agreement with it.
examples: The man they stopped answered to the description of the thief.

oewn-00720232-v.learner: to act in reply to something that acts on you, or to an order you are given.
examples: The horse answered the rein at once and turned left.
She puzzled over his strange behaviour for days before she could answer it in her own mind.

oewn-02769539-n.learner: a small vehicle with four wheels that you push a baby or young child around in.
examples: She pushed the baby along the path in its carriage.

oewn-02972469-n.learner: a part of a machine that carries some other part.
examples: The typewriter carriage slid back to the left at the end of each line.

oewn-01064577-v.learner: to move something from one person or place to another.
examples: The spy sent the secret papers off to a foreign country.

oewn-01954657-v.learner: to move goods from one place to another as a business.
examples: The factory sends its cloth by rail to the ports.

oewn-01091334-v.learner: to give someone a post or place where they must be and do their work.
examples: The young officer was sent to a fort on the border, where he served for two years.

oewn-02353564-v.learner: to have a person taken in by an institution, such as a prison or a hospital.
examples: The judge sent him to prison for five years.

oewn-00975088-v.learner: to send out sound or pictures through the air, as by radio or television.
examples: The radio station sends the news every hour.

oewn-04893841-n.learner: the quality of being pushed to try hard because you hate to fall below your own standards.
examples: Pride kept her working late until the job was done well.
A pride of lions rested in the shade of the trees.

oewn-06216535-n.learner: a way of thinking about someone that shows you admire them or think well of them.
examples: She always spoke of the old doctor with great regard.

oewn-06643134-n.learner: a polite way of saying that you wish someone well.
examples: Please give my regards to your mother.

oewn-05710673-n.learner: the act of paying special attention to someone, for example to children or people who cannot help themselves.
examples: The nurse kept careful regard over the small children in her care.

oewn-00880326-n.learner: a long look that stays fixed on something.
examples: He turned his steady regard on the stranger at the door.
Their aunt kept a good table, and her guests always ate well.

oewn-08283156-n.learner: facts or numbers set out in rows and columns.
examples: The table at the back of the book lists the dates of each king.

oewn-09374802-n.learner: a high, flat piece of land with steep sides.
examples: The rocky table rose steeply from the desert floor.

oewn-09938220-n.learner: a person who belongs to a clan or tribe.
examples: The old stories tell how the children of Israel wandered in the desert.

oewn-13950416-n.learner: the way things are in general, or all the things that are happening together at one time.
examples: The situation in the city grew worse each day.

oewn-14434647-n.learner: a problem that is complicated, serious, or unusual.
examples: The flood created a situation the town had never faced before.

oewn-00721155-v.learner: to respond well to something, or to think that it is right and proper.
examples: At first people would not accept music that sounded so strange.

oewn-00670723-v.learner: to put up with something, or to get used to it and fit yourself to it.
examples: She had to accept the long hours and the low pay.

oewn-02241406-v.learner: to let someone come into a group or community.
examples: The college accepted only twenty new students this year.

oewn-02214718-v.learner: to use something, or to take it, for some purpose.
examples: The shop accepts cards as well as cash.

oewn-02306786-v.learner: to take on another person's costs or debts as your own.
examples: I'll accept the charges for the call.

oewn-02747421-v.learner: to be made so that it can hold or take something.
examples: This lamp accepts only small bulbs.

oewn-02215404-v.learner: to receive a report in an official way, for example one from a committee.
examples: The board voted to accept the committee's report.

oewn-00720413-v.learner: of a female farm or pet animal, to be willing to mate.
examples: The mare would not accept the stallion.

oewn-13425421-n.learner: a record in which a business writes down its money accounts.
examples: The clerk kept the shop's books neat and up to date.

oewn-07970797-n.learner: a set of rules or fixed standards that decisions are based on.
examples: They run things by the book around here.

oewn-02873887-n.learner: a number of sheets, such as tickets or stamps, joined together along one edge.
examples: He bought a book of stamps at the post office.

oewn-06649049-n.learner: a collection of all the facts that are known about something or someone.
examples: The police kept a thick book on every man in the gang.

oewn-07023062-n.learner: the written words of a play or other show, used when getting ready to perform it.
examples: The actors still had their books in their hands at the first rehearsal.

oewn-07971027-n.learner: a group of playing cards that meets what the rules of a card game require.
examples: In bridge, the first six tricks you win make up your book.
